analysis.title: Americas Energy: Oil & Gas - E&P: Permian Basin Takeaways: Highlight Buys on PR For FCF Per Share Growth and FANG for Organic Midland Asset Value
key_insights: GS met Permian Resources (PR, Buy) and Diamondback Energy (FANG, Buy) in Midland on November 11 and left incrementally positive on both. The note highlights PR for FCF per share growth and FANG for organic Midland asset value.
PR management is focused on compounding FCF per share through the cycle. In 3Q26 PR generated $0.98 of FCF per share at ~$86/bbl WTI, up from $0.88 in 2Q26 at ~$93/bbl WTI.

GS sees PR's FCF per share growth coming from strong oil production, operational efficiencies, a meaningful natural gas sales inflection and continued ground game (bolt-on acquisition) success. Exhibit 1 shows a GSe FCF/share CAGR of almost 20% from 2025-2028.

GS left the PR meeting with more confidence that oil and gas assets on federal lands (New Mexico) will not be materially impacted by policy. Investor attention to the risk could rise after the mid-term elections, but GS's base case is limited impact on value.

PR kept executing its ground game despite higher oil prices in 2026. About $2.20 bn of transactions were announced year-to-date as of 3Q26 earnings. In January, at WTI of $56.97/bbl, PR had said it was willing to consolidate the Delaware Basin in softer macro environments.

On the Ridge Runner deal, PR said contingent payments that share upside in higher oil prices helped close the agreement. PR also cited the affiliated royalties business, which raises the NRI of the acreage. PR sees a 3-5 year runway of Delaware Basin consolidation opportunities.

FANG removed the percent-of-FCF target from its return of capital framework alongside 1Q26 earnings in May. This gives management more flexibility for counter-cyclical buybacks. Management reiterated a willingness to buy back stock opportunistically when it screens cheap on internal metrics.
FANG repurchased shares at average prices of ~$187 in 2Q26 and ~$186 in 3Q26. GS calls the stock attractive at $180.98, a 14% FCF yield on GS's 2028 estimates.

GS sees FANG shifting toward organic development after a successful M&A record. The Barnett offers longer-duration upside as development costs fall and competes for capital within the portfolio. FANG cited scarce acreage in the market combining quality resource, undeveloped locations and oil-focused economics, and expects a greater focus on organic development over the next decade.

FANG's new partnership with KKR to jointly acquire Five Point Infrastructure's 70% stake in Deep Blue is meant to address in-basin water-management constraints. Management said greater strategic control of Deep Blue is an advantage of the structure. FANG is investing in in-basin infrastructure to become a partner for data center end markets.

Exhibit 3 says FANG has lagged on M&A concerns and a shareholder overhang, but GS expects a more organic approach to value creation for now. Exhibit 4 says FANG's oil productivity execution is improving versus Midland peer wells despite the basin maturing.

market_movers.rationale: 12-month PT is based on a target FCF yield of 11.5% on 2027/2028 estimates, with 85% weight on ~$231 fundamental value and 15% on ~$259 M&A value. GS highlights organic Midland asset value and buyback flexibility.

12-month PT is based on a target FCF yield of 12.5% on 2027/2028 estimates, with 85% weight on ~$28 fundamental value and 15% on ~$32 M&A value. GS highlights FCF per share growth and ground game execution.

sector_views.rationale: GS highlights Buys on PR and FANG. It sees limited policy impact on federal-lands value and expects a gas sales inflection and operational efficiencies to support FCF per share.

earnings_insights: PR 3Q26 FCF per share was $0.98 at ~$86/bbl WTI (reported, as cited by GS), versus $0.88 in 2Q26 at ~$93/bbl WTI.
PR has announced ~$2.20 bn of transactions year-to-date as of 3Q26 earnings. GS sees a 3-5 year runway of Delaware Basin consolidation.
FANG repurchased stock at average prices of ~$187 in 2Q26 and ~$186 in 3Q26. FANG released productivity data alongside 3Q26 earnings, which GS cites for the Barnett.
GS forecasts PR FCF/share CAGR of almost 20% from 2025-2028 (GSe, ex-working capital), with natural gas sales net of processing costs rising as gas realizations improve.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Price environment cited for PR's $0.98 of FCF per share in 3Q26, down from ~$93/bbl in 2Q26.
Oil deck behind the FANG and PR price targets.
Gas deck behind the price targets. Improving gas realizations support PR's cash flow inflection.

risk_factors: Key risks to both FANG and PR price targets: costs, well results, commodity price volatility and government pronouncements.
Federal lands policy risk in New Mexico could draw more investor attention after the mid-term elections.
Higher oil prices make acquisition economics harder for PR's inorganic consolidation.
FANG has lagged on M&A concerns and a shareholder overhang.

tension_points.bull_case: GS's base case is limited impact on value from policy. After meeting PR it has greater confidence that oil and gas business value on federal lands will not be materially impacted.
tension_points.bear_case: Investor attention around federal lands risk in New Mexico could increase on the back of the mid-term elections. GS has been receiving investor inbounds on tail risks to operating assets on federal lands.
